views.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Proceed with the already-finalized $50B Section 301 tariff schedule as leverage — the 25% List 1 tariffs land July 6 — but hold the line on posture: do not immediately trigger the additional ~$200B of tariffs or broaden the fight, and keep negotiation channels open so China can trade concrete structural concessions on IP/technology transfer for relief. This is a hold stance, not escalation and not unilateral concession.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: The threat to US interests is modest — toward opportunity, not danger. The US is the initiator holding the initiative (Section 301 finding, ZTE denial order April 16, final $50B plan June 15), and the macro backdrop is strong: industrial production at 103.4 and rising, fed funds up from 1.42% to 1.91%, broad dollar up ~3.4%, consumer sentiment ~98 — the dispute is not yet biting the US real economy. That supports a mild threat_score of about -0.15 (leverage, onshoring, tough-on-China politics) rather than a high reading. But the downside risk is real and rising: China matched the $50B step-for-step with $34B of retaliation effective the same day (June 15), scrapping the May 19 purchase deal, and targeted the farm belt — $14B of US soybean exports, futures at a one-year low — precisely in battleground states ahead of the November midterms, as Republican senators and the Iowa Soybean Association have warned. That domestic political and escalation-spiral exposure argues against pushing harder right now; conversely, the leverage and absence of material economic damage argue against rolling back before China delivers structural reform. The coherent stance is hold: let the committed tariffs land as leverage, refrain from the $200B escalation that would deepen farm-belt pain and market volatility, and keep talks open (action_score 0.0).
key_factors: US is initiator with strong economy and strong dollar (3.4% broad-dollar rise) — leverage terrain, not existential threat
IP/industrial-production metrics healthy; tariffs not yet damaging US macro
China matched $50B with same-day $34B retaliation on soybeans/autos/ag and scrapped May 19 purchase deal
China targets $14B soybean export / GOP farm-belt base ahead of 2018 midterms — political and spiral risk
Threat of $200B additional tariffs raises escalation-spiral and market-volatility downside
